articles.title: James Cameron Congratulates Marvel After Avengers: Endgame Beats Avatar at the Box Office Yet Again
articles.summary: James Cameron celebrated Avengers: Endgame beating Avatar at the box office with another social media post after the two movies traded places yet again. The director behind the smash-hit sci-fi franchise brought Iron Man to the world of Pandora with an image he shared on Instagram today.
body: "'You are one of the people,'" the post, accompanied by a picture of Iron Man surrounded by Na'vi, said. "Congratulations to Marvel and the #1 Avengers: Endgame: Encore for bringing moviegoers to the cinemas – Jim Cameron."

It's more friendly competition in the movie space that is only the latest update in a race that has seen Avatar and Avengers: Endgame trading titles for years. Marvel originally overtook Avatar's record as the highest-grossing movie in the world when it released in 2019. Cameron shared a similarly congratulatory post at the time but later went on to predict that Avatar would reclaim the throne just a few months later. He was proven right in 2021.

As Avatar sequels The Way of Water and Fire and Ash came and went, so too did more Marvel Cinematic Universe movies. As Marvel prepared for the release of its new team-up movie, Avengers: Doomsday, this December, it saw an opportunity to revisit the events of Endgame with new bonus footage, thrusting it into the future by revisiting the past.
points: James Cameron celebrated Avengers: Endgame beating Avatar at the box office with another social media post after the two movies traded places yet again.
"'You are one of the people,'" the post, accompanied by a picture of Iron Man surrounded by Na'vi, said.
"Congratulations to Marvel and the #1 Avengers: Endgame: Encore for bringing moviegoers to the cinemas – Jim Cameron."

articles.title: Ben Affleck's Batman Movie Would Have Featured Arkham Asylum-Inspired Deathstroke Fight and DCEU Batgirl, Joe Manganiello Reveals
articles.summary: Joe Manganiello has revealed new plot details about Ben Affleck's canceled Batman movie, including information about an Arkham Asylum-inspired fight with Deathstroke and the DCEU's Batgirl.
body: The actor, who was cast as Slade Wilson before the comic book movie universe was rebooted with the DCU, talked about his time working with Affleck on the canned project in his new book, Bloodlines: A Memoir. Entertainment Weekly shared excerpts from the book, which said the Batman movie would have been packed with reveals – and even a death – for some of Bruce Wayne's closest allies.

Affleck's plan for his standalone Caped Crusader flick would have seen Batman primarily tangling with Deathstroke after the character was first teased in a Justice League end-credits sequence. He described the narrative as "a superhero version of David Fincher's The Game" focused on Deathstroke trying to "dismantle Batman's entire life."

This is a plot description Manganiello has shared before, but now we know that the iconic DC villain had it out for Batman because he had been led to believe that he murdered his son. Affleck's Bruce Wayne has been known to take lives in the past, but how involved he would have been with the killing of Slade's son is unclear. It sounds like that wouldn't have stopped Deathstroke from tearing Gotham apart to get revenge.

articles.title: 5 Years Later, One Game’s Blood Sacrifice Mechanic Still Haunts Me
articles.summary: Typically, when you’re playing a card game, the stakes aren’t that high. Perhaps you’ve got some money on the line. Maybe bragging rights are on the table. But even if you lose, largely speaking, things are going to be fine.
body: So is your host. Leshy, the forest-dwelling hermit across the table, makes his living photographing animals with a magic camera and turning their essences into playing cards. To get out, you’re going to have to beat Leshy at his own game. Just make sure he doesn’t turn you into a card before you figure out a way to escape.

In the first act of Inscryption, you’re playing a tabletop card battler against Leshy, one match at a time. Each creature card has an attack and a health stat. You place your cards in lanes across from his. Determine your play, ring a bell, and your chosen cards attack. Any creature nobody’s blocking deals damage, tracked as teeth on an ominous nearby scale. Earn five teeth, and you win the round. Each card you’d want to play has a price: Blood, usually.
points: Typically, when you’re playing a card game, the stakes aren’t that high.
But even if you lose, largely speaking, things are going to be fine.

articles.title: Tim Burton's 77-Minute Stop-Motion Masterpiece Is Officially Back on Streaming
articles.summary: When it comes to beautiful, high-quality stop-motion animation, independent studio Laika is the first name that comes to mind. The studio’s hand-crafted puppetry and 3D-printing technology have brought beautiful tales to life for years, from Coraline to ParaNorman.
body: Yet as much a technical and emotional achievement as Wildwood has proven to be, you don’t need to head to your local theater to see Laika's best animated film. All you need to do is go to HBO Max, where Tim Burton ’s masterful 2005 Corpse Bride is streaming right now.

Directed by Tim Burton and Mike Johnson, Corpse Bride follows Victor Van Dort (Johnny Depp) and his arranged marriage to Victoria Everglot (Emily Watson). After a terrible rehearsal dinner, Victor heads to the woods to practice his vows. Without thinking, he says them aloud and slips his ring onto what he believes is a tree branch sticking out from the ground. But the “branch” is actually the finger of an undead bride, Emily (Helena Bonham Carter), who immediately assumes they’re engaged. Victor is soon dragged into the land of the dead, where he comes face-to-face with its inhabitants.
points: When it comes to beautiful, high-quality stop-motion animation, independent studio Laika is the first name that comes to mind.
The studio’s hand-crafted puppetry and 3D-printing technology have brought beautiful tales to life for years, from Coraline to ParaNorman.

articles.title: The Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Sounds Meaningfully Better Than the Original
articles.summary: Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here.
body: Guess what — Nintendo's all-in on physical media. This unsurprising fact became news this week after an executive for Nintendo in Latin America made some mild and extremely uncontroversial comments to the effect. "We know how much the fans like it," Bill van Zyll said, while pointing out that the company had just launched a new platform, in Switch 2, that supports physical cartridges. This is only worth noting due to Sony's unpopular decision to end production of physical PlayStation games starting in 2028, but still: good to know.

As a family-oriented company which still has strong ties to toy retail, Nintendo enjoys a far higher proportion of physical retail sales than any of its competitors, so this position just makes a boring kind of sense. But it also has more to lose; as pressure on memory chip prices continues, Switch game cards are surely much more expensive to manufacture than Blu-ray discs. Hence the functionally empty game-key cards most third-party publishers have resorted to. But when it comes to its own titles, Nintendo still insists on shipping the full game on the card, and hang the expense.

articles.title: Qualcomm wins $2 legal decision against fellow tech giant Arm, and that's not a typo
articles.summary: At a glance: Qualcomm gets $2 from Arm in the Delaware jury's decision, part of a yearslong licensing dispute between the two. Yahoo Finance puts their market caps at $210 billion and $243 billion respectively.
body: Reuters reported on the mystifying reward, which makes much more sense in the context of a broader legal battle between Qualcomm and Arm. The two companies are each behind some of the most widely-used processors in the world: Qualcomm's Snapdragon CPUs can be found in most non-Apple smartphones. Arm's titular architecture, meanwhile, is the basis of the Snapdragon CPU, and there are rumblings the future of desktop computing belongs to Arm and not the x86 architecture we've defaulted to for so long.

The Delaware jury found that Arm breached a licensing agreement with Qualcomm, failing to provide patches and support for designs Qualcomm had licensed. The jury also ruled in favor of Qualcomm's allegation that Arm strategically leaked information to Bloomberg News that delayed a deal between Qualcomm and Meta in 2024. The jury sided with Arm over Qualcomm on five other counts.

The big prize for Qualcomm would be proving Arm acted in bad faith after licensing its technology out, activating a five-year freeze on royalty payments specified in the companies' original agreement⁠—that could be worth billions of dollars.

articles.title: 'I am overwhelmed and overstimulated': The actor behind Star Wars: Galactic Racer’s Biddy Blas is scribbing doon all your enthusiasm
articles.summary: Every time I check in on Star Wars, there's a new stupid little creature (colloquially known as a Glup Shitto) everyone's into. The latest of these is Biddy Blas, a braggadocious pod racer and mama's boy who stands out for his shrill Huttese quips. "Ding dong pookie, ding dong," he crows.
body: If you hate that, here's a video of him dying in a fireball.

He's become the subject of meme after meme and people generally like the little brat. The voice actor for Biddy Blas, a British wrestler named Richard Summers-Calvert, has responded to all the love—and as you might guess, he basically looks like the opposite of Biddy Blas. All the attention has left him "overwhelmed and overstimulated," as he said in a video he shared on X, and he's hoping to show up for new fans of the Shitto du jour at cons and the like.

In a follow-up video, he said he had some "good news" that he wasn't ready to announce just yet, and thanked all the Biddy-heads for the doors a sudden spotlight like this opens. "I know you're doing it for Biddy. I know you're doing it for him. But I benefit from him as well … I appreciate all the love. And hate, and frustration." It is a racing game, after all.

articles.summary: Sega and Creative Assembly are temporarily removing Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from sale just days after release.
body: In a statement shared on Twitter/X, the companies said they are aware the game "has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards".
"We've seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be," the statement continued.
The companies are working "with platform holders to temporarily remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues".
"Existing owners will still be able to access and play the game," the statement added.

articles.title: Gameplay footage emerges of reportedly cancelled Assassin's Creed game Destiny
articles.summary: Footage of a reportedly cancelled Assassin's Creed game set in ancient China has emerged online, including stealth kills, the series' leap of faith, and a spinning umbrella weapon.
body: Called Assassin's Creed Destiny, it was reportedly being made for current platforms at Tencent -owned TiMi Studio Group, which also worked on mobile game Assassin's Creed Jade.

According to MP1st, the clips were taken from portfolios belonging to people who worked on it, and most come from a prototype built in February 2025. It's thought Destiny's setting was 206 BCE, nine years after Jade's 215 BCE.

The main mission has a female assassin heading into a sacred palace under siege from the army of the warlord Xiang Yu, in search of a mysterious artefact, and an early-stage boss encounter involving the warlord also appears.

Elsewhere, a male character uses parkour to dispatch enemies, while a temporary test area shows the player using an umbrella-style spinning weapon, with ink-brush ability icons and a health bar on screen.

articles.title: Surprising no-one, Wizards of the Coast 'doesn't intend to voluntarily recognize' union efforts for the second time this year
articles.summary: Per the United Wizards of the Coast Union (UWOTC-CWA) account on X, WoTC is acting in an entirely unsurprising manner: "Yesterday, Wizards informed us that it doesn’t intend to voluntarily recognize the D&D or Studio X units of our union ahead of a vote.
body: A union composed of employees from the Magic: The Gathering Arena team unionised back in June of this year, giving WoTC until May to formally recognise it. Obviously, it didn't.

Later in the same month, WoTC sent physical letters to members of the company encouraging them not to go through with it on the vote—and while WoTC did technically adhere to the The National Labor Relations Act, it did also not-so-subtly imply that its current benefits would be "on the bargaining table for both parties to negotiate". These letters were also allegedly accompanied by daily emails to employees.

Basically, it should not come as a surprise that Wizards isn't intending to recognize the full United Wizards of the Coast Union—a coalition now formed of members in both the D&D team and Studio X (Magic: The Gathering's creative staff)—either.

"We are best able to keep building great games and a great place to work by working directly with employees, not through unions. In this regard, Wizards is not neutral on the question of unionization … in the end, we will respect the results of the election, no matter what our employees choose."

articles.title: Discussion time: Do you think zone chats in MMOs are forces for good, or evil?
articles.summary: Terminally Online. This is Terminally Online: PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about…
body: Ah, zone chats in MMOs—trade and general chats, /shouts and /yells. Intended as a way to render the social glue that binds these videogames together, they are often instead a tableau for (and I say this somewhat affectionately) absolute lunacy, pock-marked with some of the most vile verbiage you'll see online.

Take, for instance, the time-honoured tradition of "Barrens Chat" in World of Warcraft. Combine a big zone that spans around 10-15 levels along with proximity to a major city, and you get a certain kind of verbal hooliganry that, in my journeys through WoW: Forever, I was actually pretty nostalgic for.

I mean, sure, the Chuck Norris jokes have gotten a smidge old. But while collecting Zhevra Hoofs, I would find myself possessed to ask Barrens Chat philosophical questions, and while I never received much in the way of wisdom, responses were always entertaining.

I'm not so fond of trade chat, though, which—at least on the horde side of things—has mostly been dominated by a bot by the name of Margrave Tyrael. Who, I kid you not, was literally sitting there for days spitting out the same automated messages, questioning why Blizzard was deleting beta characters.

body: Well, that came out of nowhere! With over a month to go until Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases, Rockstar has blessed us with an actual launch trailer.
